walkthroughs.body_html:
Philosophy of Religion: Problems of Evil & Suffering — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Philosophy of Religion: Problems of Evil & Suffering brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Philosophy of Religion: Problems of Evil & Suffering.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does Mackie's logical problem of evil claim?
options: That God's omnipotence, God's goodness and the existence of evil cannot all be true together
That evil is an illusion
That suffering proves there are many gods
That natural evil does not exist

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of moral evil?
options: Genocide
A tsunami
A drought
An earthquake

mcqs.q: In Hick's theodicy, what is 'epistemic distance'?
options: God remains hidden enough for humans to choose faith and goodness freely
The physical distance between heaven and earth
The gap between rich and poor
The distance between galaxies

mcqs.q: What does the free will defence argue?
options: Genuine freedom is so valuable that God is justified in permitting the evil its misuse brings
Humans have no free will
God causes every evil act directly
Freedom only exists in heaven

mcqs.q: Is the problem of evil only about logical contradiction?
options: Once the logical problem is answered, the problem of evil is completely solved.
The problem of evil was first invented in the twentieth century.

No - the evidential version, pressed by Rowe with cases like a fawn dying slowly in a forest fire, argues that apparently pointless suffering makes God improbable even if no strict contradiction exists.
Hick argued that suffering is a punishment for past lives.

mcqs.q: Does soul-making neatly explain every amount of suffering?
options: No - critics object that some evil crushes rather than develops people and seems excessive; Hick himself appeals to mystery and universal salvation to respond.
Hick's theodicy shows that every instance of suffering produces growth.
Hick argued that suffering is a punishment for past lives.
The problem of evil was first invented in the twentieth century.

mcqs.q: Did Augustine teach that God created evil?
options: No - for Augustine creation was 'very good' and evil is a privation arising from free creatures turning away from God, not a substance God made.
Augustine denied that anyone ever suffers.
The problem of evil was first invented in the twentieth century.
Augustine believed God deliberately built evil into creation.

free_texts.hint: Student of Socrates, teacher of Aristotle.

sequence.def: c.300 BC: evil challenges divine power and love
c.180 AD: growth from image to likeness of God
c.400 AD: evil as privation after the Fall
1710: this is the best of all possible worlds
